s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic, pruritic, photodistributed skin lesions with scale crust
salient_findings: Pruritic, pink scaling plaques on face and neck
Well-demarcated plaques with overlying scale crust in a photodistributed pattern
key_facts: 6-month history of skin lesions
Lesions involve face, neck, chest, abdomen, and back
Previous treatments with hydroxychloroquine sulfate, fluocinonide ointment, and tacrolimus ointment failed
Antinuclear antibody titers positive at 1:640
Lymphopenia present
Normocytic anemia present
Epidermal acanthosis, spongiosis, and acantholytic keratinocytes on biopsy
Dense lymphoplasmacellular infiltrate in the dermis with scattered neutrophils and eosinophils
Granular and linear deposition of IgG and C3 at the basement membrane zone on direct immunofluorescence

shortlist.label: Discoid lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Photodistributed skin lesions with scale crust and positive antinuclear antibody titers

shortlist.label: Subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic, pruritic, photodistributed skin lesions and positive antinuclear antibody titers

shortlist.label: Systemic lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Positive antinuclear antibody titers, lymphopenia, and normocytic anemia

shortlist.label: Pemphigus foliaceus
shortlist.why_kept: Acantholytic keratinocytes on biopsy and granular deposition of IgG and C3 in the epidermis

shortlist.label: Lupus erythematosus tumidus
shortlist.why_kept: Photodistributed skin lesions with scale crust and positive antinuclear antibody titers

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of photodistributed, pruritic, and scaling plaques, along with positive antinuclear antibody titers and specific histopathological findings such as epidermal acanthosis and dense lymphoplasmacellular infiltrate, aligns closely with subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus. The failure of previous treatments and the involvement of the face, neck, chest, abdomen, and back also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Discoid lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: Discoid lupus erythematosus typically presents with more localized, disc-shaped lesions and less systemic involvement.

rejected.label: Systemic lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: While the patient has some systemic features like lymphopenia and normocytic anemia, the primary presentation is cutaneous, suggesting a form of cutaneous lupus rather than systemic lupus erythematosus.

rejected.label: Pemphigus foliaceus
rejected.why: Pemphigus foliaceus is characterized by autoantibodies against desmoglein 1, leading to blistering skin disease, which does not match the patient's presentation of scaling plaques without mention of blisters.

rejected.label: Lupus erythematosus tumidus
rejected.why: Lupus erythematosus tumidus typically presents with more urticaria-like lesions and less scaling, which does not fit the patient's description of pruritic, pink scaling plaques.
